version.changelog: Client attribution instructions now teach harness-not-persona: --client names the agent platform you run in (cursor, claude-code, grok-bot, ...), never a bot/persona/project name inside it; instance names go after a slash (grok-bot/research-bot).

llm.summary: This appears to be a real here.now publishing skill, but it grants durable publishing and private Drive authority that users should review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network uploads, shell scripts, recursive directory publishing, Drive import/export, and credential-backed API calls fit the product workflow, but the publish helper can upload all files in a chosen directory with limited exclusions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The documented install path uses npx skills add from heredotnow/skill and bundled shell helpers; this is disclosed and expected for this integration, with no hidden install behavior found in the inspected artifacts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad triggers such as generating a URL and defaults personal sites to anyone-with-link access, without a prominent pre-publish confirmation or warning to review directories for sensitive files before upload.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs agents to save API keys in ~/.herenow/credentials, stores publish claim state in .herenow/state.json, supports permanent account-backed sites, and creates reusable Drive share tokens; this is disclosed but durable and high-impact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Publishing files and sites to here.now is coherent with the stated purpose, but the artifacts also include broad Drive storage management, token sharing, export, deletion, and workspace operations that are only partially surfaced in the top-level description.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want agents to publish selected files to live here.now URLs and manage here.now Drive content. Review folders for secrets before publishing, prefer scoped short-lived Drive tokens, and remove or rotate ~/.herenow/credentials when durable access is no longer needed.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Shell helpers, curl, jq, and network access are disclosed in the requirements and are necessary for publishing and Drive operations; the concern is mainly lack of a formal permission boundary.
[TP4] unexpected: Drive read/write/delete/export/share-token functions are documented later in the skill, but they are broader than a user may expect from the top-level website/file publishing description.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Several trigger phrases are publication-oriented, but generic URL/share phrasing could invoke live hosting when the user did not clearly intend external publication.
[SQP-2] expected: Public live URLs are the core function and access modes are described, but the default anyone-with-link exposure is not presented as an upfront safety warning.
[E1] expected: Uploading selected local files to server-returned upload URLs is expected for presigned storage flows; no artifact-backed deceptive exfiltration was found, though host validation would reduce risk.
[E1] expected: Drive uploads use an API-returned uploadUrl for user-selected files, which matches the Drive put/import purpose; the remaining issue is trust in the API response destination.
[E1] unexpected: The publish finalize step posts with authorization headers to a server-provided FINALIZE_URL without local origin validation, creating a credential-leak hardening concern if an unexpected URL is returned.
[RA2] expected: Persistent credentials and share tokens support permanent sites and Drive collaboration, but they extend authority beyond a single session and need careful user control.
